notes.title: One Last Demo Update
notes.notes:
[p]Hello friends,[/p][p][/p][p]I've released one last awesome update for the demo before proceeding with work on the full version of Sick Samurai. This will be the last major update for the demo until we participate in Next Fest in many months from now. Stay tuned for updates on full version progress coming very soon![/p][p][/p][p][b]Update notes below:[/b][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]The Katsuryoku Sake upgrade (reduced attack/dodge cooldowns) has been replaced with the Zenshin Sake upgrade. This upgrade will cause time to slow down when you dodge, making the dodge significantly more powerful and giving you ample time to set up sick plays. The slowmo slowly fades, and will be cancelled instantly when you attack, use an item, or press the dodge button again.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]The Stun Bomb is now called the Whistle Bomb and is significantly more powerful. It will kill all enemies in a small radius around the blast while stunning remaining enemies that are a bit further away.
[/p][/*][*][p]The power of the Whistle Bomb is balanced by its inventory slot usage. It requires 2 slots to equip 1 whistle bomb, while the kunai still only requires 1 slot per kunai.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Attack ranges and enemy targeting have been modified to make the difference between a successful attack and a miss as clear as possible[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]You can now instantly unequip and fully equip all kunai/bombs by clicking on their icon in the backpack instead of incrementing/decrementing them one by one.
[/p][/*][*][p]There is now an additional graphics setting called "Ultra Low". On top of all the other things the lower graphics settings disable, this mode will also disable all postprocessing fx. [/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]A variety of other performance optimizations have been made that are applicable to all graphics settings.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]I hope you enjoy these changes, they're a lot of fun, and I hope you'll hear from me again very soon.[/p][p][/p][p]Solideo[/p]

notes.title: Sick Samurai Demo 2.0 Is Now Live!
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey everyone,[/h1][h3][/h3][p][/p][p]First, a big thank you to everyone who's played and wishlisted the game so far! The reception has been very positive and I'm glad to see so many people digging it.[/p][p][/p][p]BUT.... alright, maybe the demo was juuuuust a little too hard for you scrubs. Just a touch.[/p][p][/p][p]After taking in all the best feedback over the past couple weeks, I'm happy to announce that a new version of the demo is now available![/p][p][/p][h3]In fact, it includes so many changes and improvements, I'm calling it Demo 2.0.[/h3][p][/p][h3][b]These changes include but are not limited to:[/b][/h3][p]
-Difficulty curves, especially for new players[/p][p]-A simplified, super easy to use control scheme[/p][p]-New mechanics around dodging and missing attacks[/p][p]-A "learn" mode for quick and easy practice and lessons[/p][p]-New achievements[/p][p]-Countless quality of life improvements[/p][p][/p][p]And for those of you with balls of steel who prefer the most relentlessly brutal version of the demo - don't worry, the option is there with all the new improvements included.[/p][p][/p][p]I hope this update will improve upon the already dope experience, and allow a wider audience to appreciate the thrill of the kill.[/p][p][/p][h3]Full list of changes below, and stay tuned for work on the full version coming soon, PEACE![/h3][p][/p][h2][b]Sick Samurai Demo 2.0 Update[/b]
[/h2][p][/p][h3][b]Gameplay changes:[/b]
[/h3][p]-Your attack range when smashing through a door is larger, so highlighted enemies are guaranteed to be hit even if they step out of range at the last moment.
[/p][p]-Missing an attack will slow down time, which will slowly transition back to normal. This effect only happens on the "Chill" and "Normal" difficulty levels. Dodging or using an item in this state will instantly restore regular time.
[/p][p]-Dodging now instantly resets your attack cooldown.
[/p][p]-The passive upgrade drink reward in the bar is no longer a movement speed upgrade - instead, it reduces your attack and dodge cooldowns.[/p][p][/p][p]-Bonus points are now awarded for blocking a kickable object with a kunai.[/p][p][/p][p]-Bonus points are awarded for destroying enemy projectiles and kickables with the Girameki technique.[/p][p][/p][p]-The Girameki technique will now allow your projectiles and kicked objects to continue on their path after time unfreezes.This allows them to hit enemies before they're killed, which then combines with the Girameki technique for extra bonus points.
[/p][p]-Slightly increased the player's maximum dash range.
[/p][p]-Dodging is now effective for using kickable objects.
[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Enemy changes:[/b]
[/h3][p]-Improved pathfinding so enemies don't get too close to obstacles or feel like they kill you through them.
[/p][p]-Patrolling enemies now walk slower.
[/p][p]-Slightly reduced enemy attack range.
[/p][p]-Enemy stats and enemy and object placements in levels have been completely redone for the "Chill" and "Normal" difficulty levels for a smoother difficulty curve for new players.
[/p][p]-The "Sick" (hard mode) difficulty option now changes the enemies and their placements to how they were in the original version of the demo.[/p][p][/p][p]-Enemies now delay their reaction to you until you've landed inside of the room (instead of reacting instantly upon clicking the door).
[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Level changes:[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]-Most obstacles have been removed. They're still visually present, but climbable instead of stopping you.
[/p][p]-The remaining intentional obstacles have been made more visually obvious, and their collision is more curved, allowing you to run along them without getting stuck.[/p][p][/p][p]-Attacking and dodging around corners and edges of obstacles is now much more forgiving. You can cut through corners and along edges, you just can't go directly through the whole obstacle.[/p][p][/p][p]-Fixed some issues where using multiple dashes very quickly as you enter a new room would incorrectly fail.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Control scheme changes:[/b][/h3][h3][/h3][p][/p][h3][b]Gamepads:[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]-Interactable objects like doors and npcs in the bar are now auto-targeted if you walk up to them and are not manually aiming.[/p][p][/p][p]-If you have no target locked, attacking will be the full distance in the direction of your movement.
[/p][p]-Dodging is always the max distance in the direction of your movement.
[/p][p]-On "Chill" difficulty, targets will be locked on to based on direction of movement without any aiming required.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Keyboard+Mouse:[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]-On "Chill" difficulty, enemies and objects are auto-targeted based on closest distance to your cursor.[/p][p][/p][p]-If there are no targets locked on, you will attack to the position of your cursor.[/p][p][/p][p]-The cursor behaves exactly like a regular mouse cursor. “Unlock cursor” and “screen cursor” toggles have been removed since they’re now pointless.
[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Settings changes:[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]-Added tooltips to the settings menu that explain the purpose of each toggle and difficulty level.
[/p][p]-Added a "swap joysticks" toggle for controllers.[/p][p][/p][p]-All difficulties are available by default.[/p][p]The three difficulties are as follows:[/p][p][b]Chill[/b] - Auto-targetting enabled (essentially aim assist training wheels). Also, slow-mo on miss is a bit longer.[/p][p][b]Normal[/b] - Auto-targetting disabled. Slow-mo on miss is a bit shorter.[/p][p][b]Sick[/b] - Auto-targetting disabled, no slow-mo on miss, faster enemies, and more challenging enemy placements.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Chapter Select Screen changes:[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]-Added a difficulty selection button.[/p][p][/p][p]-Selected chapters now show the score and time needed to get a perfect rating. Different for "Sick" difficulty vs. other difficulties.[/p][p][/p][p]-Added a "prologue" button if you have chapter 1 selected[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Misc changes:[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]-[/b]The HUD now includes a cooldown meter for the dodge[/p][p][/p][p]-Made the music start playing again faster when it finishes in a level.
[/p][p]-Removed the "instant action" mode.
[/p][p]-Starting a new game will prompt you to select a difficulty. Difficulty can be changed at anytime in the settings menu.
[/p][p]-When playing for the first time, you'll be prompted to turn on hints and tips. Besides basic stuff, these tips include details on the score system and hints for higher-level strategies. Can be turned on anytime in Settings > More.[/p][p][/p][p]-Added a new "Learn" mode to the main menu. It immediately loads you into the first combat level and shows you all the tutorials, tips, and hints while you play. Enemies will not react to or kill you in this mode.[/p]

notes.title: THE DEMO IS OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
I'm excited to announce that Sick Samurai's demo has officially been released! I did everything I could to make this demo as polished, fully-featured, and replayable as possible, and I think everyone is in for a real treat. I hope you all enjoy it!

Although I'm mostly a solo developer, no game is ever truly made by just one person, so I'd like to give a big shout out to everyone who's helped me make this game into a reality so far:

Amanda Rey - Artist, produced all character sprites and designs, environments, UI, promotional materials, etc. pretty much every piece of art both in and out of the game

Maria Rincón - Animator, produced all of the game's animations

Lorenzo Morselli - Sound Designer, produced all of the game's sound fx

David Cook - Voice Actor, Jones

Starfall PR, Pieter van Hulst + team - Promo campaign for the demo

Sara Herrera - Spanish localization
Steve Ang - Chinese localization
Yui N - Japanese localization
Mel B - German localization
@giorgia40 - Italian localization
Furkan @furkankadirr - Turkish localization
Kamil P. @kamilpilip - Polish localization
Thiago dos Santos Mania - Portuguese-BR localization
Alexis Nguyen - French localization
Anna @aniakk - Russian localization

And to everyone in my discord who played the demo early and helped me put the finishing touches on it!

notes.title: Ever closer to a demo...
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

Here's where Sick Samurai's at at the beginning of February.

Everything is about getting the demo done and released as soon as possible. I've got about a week of visual polish work left to do, and all that's left after that is the audio - a handful of music tracks and sound fx, the recording of the voice lines, and the final mixing of it all. I expect it'll take me just over a month to get that all done. Finally, we'll do a week or two of private playtesting, and the public release will follow immediately after that - so you can expect to be playing no later than April!

In the meantime, we've finished designing all of the enemies and characters for the game's second act. This act features a style inspired by Western and Japanese hip hop cultures, mid 20th-century jazz culture, yakuza and island-wear influences, and a touch of the 1970s.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45268489/036a7ee8d440a4915bf258b54f9b8c03ed0c2dbb.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45268489/5aa44561683f7b01bfe9b34f4095e17a9c5cf1b0.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45268489/05f1d6a2aaf4667408ef18b0fcb63052bbb28508.png[/img]

This act also features two samurai boss characters:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45268489/5ec79ac95e8e88caabbbabb36aee84e62f0996da.png[/img]

Damien is Jones' (the bartender) younger brother and the ruler of the island's city. He's known for his unusual style of dual-wielding katanas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45268489/178241ce8f778b57f8e368cd30eff94b3c437a05.png[/img]

Violet is Damien's partner in ruling as well as being his questionable romantic interest. She prefers to fight from a distance, using a miniature crossbow and throwing knives, though she also keeps a long dagger on hand just in case.

I hope to have most of the soundtrack done by the next time I post, and thanks for all the interest and support!

Until then,
Solideo

notes.title: Sick Samurai's Development Plans!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

I'm Solideo, a solo developer from Montreal, and I wanted to give you a big thank you for all the interest you've shown in my upcoming game, Sick Samurai. In just two weeks of being on Steam, we've already gotten 2000 wishlists!

For this project, I'm collaborating with a few people:

Artist Amanda Rey ([url=https://amandarey.art/]https://amandarey.art/[/url])

Animator Maria Rincon ([url=https://mariarinconnav.com/]https://mariarinconnav.com/[/url])

Sound Designer Lorenzo Morselli ([url=https://lorenzomorselli.webflow.io/]https://lorenzomorselli.webflow.io/[/url])

The next step in development is to get a demo out there, and I expect to release that in about 3 months. The game's story is told in 3 acts, and the demo will contain the first half of the first act (4 gameplay levels and a few narrative scenes). I hope to make it as excellent of an experience for you as I can!

Outside of that, I will be posting regular updates on the game's development both here and on various other platforms ([url=https://linktr.ee/solideo_games]https://linktr.ee/solideo_games[/url]) on a bi-weekly or monthly basis.

This week, I've got two new major characters to introduce you to:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45268489/32fc3699cf905076997145697f4f840915652174.png[/img]
[b]Dhalia[/b], the first lady of the roster. Much like Jones, Dhalia grew up an orphan surviving on the streets of the island. As a woman in an underworld largely dominated by men, she learned to carry a ferocious attitude, and developed a reputation for unpredictability and, to put it crudely, craziness. Instead of joining a gang, she mostly worked alone, and made her living blackmailing the rich, criminal or otherwise. Those who cross her will learn of her expertise in poisons and explosives. If she teams up with somebody else, it’s almost always Jones – perhaps the only man in the underworld that she gets along with. We're grateful to have Dhalia on the team, as it was becoming a bit of a sausage fest – and speaking of sausages, that brings us to our next major character.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45268489/541a8382a13bc2987a3061dbf5e2ef69bd16c03c.png[/img]
[b]Samurai Gomen[/b]. Gomen is the first of the four samurai bosses you will challenge. Delusional about his superiority over others and incapable of admitting to a single flaw within himself. He carries himself with an unearned arrogance, but he is surprisingly kind, generous, and charismatic, so long as you aren't the target of his insults, mockery, and lecturing. He represses any show of genuine emotion, alternating between apathy and a fake cheerfulness. When challenged, he maintains an unsettling, silent calmness, but if pushed too far, he explodes with rage. And don't be fooled by his size – he moves much faster than you'd expect. 

I'm excited to share more with you all soon!

Yours truly,
Solideo
